title: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer
titleZh: GLM-5.4: Toward generalized coding with our first loop transformer
author: foohis
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: HarHarVeryFunny
comments.textRawHtml:
I love the transparency, or at least given technical details, that Zhipu provide - a refreshing change from the locked-down approach of the western companies, and an interesting glimpse into the direction of SOTA LLMs.

Looped Transformers are an obvious direction even if there are still problems to be worked out. The original Transformer is a bit like an unrolled for loop, and rather unnaturally pairs different sets of weights, both for attention and feed forward (knowledge) with different "layers" (aka loop iterations). Far more natural is to strive for something more like our brain's thalamo-cortical loop and association cortex, where "thought" is iterative and there are no restrictions as to what patterns/knowledge get applied when.

A similar idea has been explored before ("Universal Transformer", 2019), seemingly going nowhere, but perhaps "necessity is the mother of invention" and compute-starved Chinese companies are finding a way to make it work.

children.author: Aurornis
children.textRawHtml:
> a refreshing change from the locked-down approach of the western companies, and an interesting glimpse into the direction of SOTA LLMs

If you haven’t seen it, Thinking Machines released an interesting looped model, open weights, last week with some interesting writeups:

https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/

To be honest, I’m getting a little tired of the “eastern vs western” discourse seeping in to so much of the LLM discourse, especially when the east versus west distinction doesn’t exist as much as implied. In this case, looped model research came out of “the west” and a “western” lab was first to release an open looped model. Can we drop the whole east versus west thing and just appreciate the progress and research?

children.author: matt_d
children.textRawHtml:
NVIDIA Megatron has been pretty open:

- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM

- https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/

Over the past few years they've been releasing papers that have been foundational for how TP and SP are being done today:

- Megatron-LM, https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08053

- Reducing Activation Recomputation, https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05198

and there's new ones, too, e.g., Scalable Training of Mixture-of-Experts Models with Megatron Core, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07685

children.textRawHtml:
For those who are in computing but not in AI, looped transformers are like chain-of-thought but for every token during every forward pass (based on the number of loops as spec'd in the model architecture), correct?

Does this mean we're opening up a whole new space of efficiency and performance gains even while keeping model sizes (chinchilla-optimal models) constant?

This is mind-blowing, though. Reality (the universe) just keeps on giving to our newfound tech tree branch of artificial neural networks.

children.author: noddybear
children.textRawHtml: A normal transformer has N layers, all of which are run forward for each token. A looped transformer is a bit different. Instead of N layers, it has K. These K layers are then looped, such that the output (not a token) of the first run of these K are fed back into the start of the K layer block. This looping happens until a fixed-point is achieved (i.e another loop results in a noop). At that point, a token is sampled. This means that tokens get different amounts of compute, depending on how challenging they are.

children.author: drakythe
children.textRawHtml: The 2x is arbitrary and in this particular case, is the fixed-point. I've seen models that do 3x loops for 3/4s of their layers. I suspect we'll see see loop counts increase as this becomes a more popular technique and may reach a point where one of the big labs is confident in their model's ability to loop "indefinitely" without becoming bogged down, reaching some logically measured point.

children.author: smallmancontrov
children.textRawHtml: "Fixed point" in the context of iterative algorithms usually means "repeat a variable number of times until the output doesn't change." This is in stark contrast to the idea of repeating a fixed number of times. The looped models appear to repeat a fixed number of times.
